utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing with the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Kapetanovic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness does not have the microphone on.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Good morning. At the end of yesterday's testimony, you had just begun to describe the events of the night of the 16th to the 17th of April, 1992, in Bosanski Samac. And you had described to the Chamber how you had been awoken by gunfire and how that, during the passage of the night from about 1.30 in the morning through to dawn, you had received various forms of information from a number of neighbours living in the same apartment block as you. And you finished by telling us that in the early morning, that the group of special units and 4th Detachment had come to the apartment block and that the person who had -- was at the entrance of your apartment was one of the defendants, Mr. Miroslav Tadic. Do you recall ending on that testimony yesterday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask if the witness could be given P68 ID? That's a diagram of Edvard Kardelj block number 62, with the ERN 02199070.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection regarding the question that my colleague from the Prosecution asked. I said that -- I don't think that the time was stated yesterday in the record when the 4th Detachment members came, and the question that the Prosecutor asked now states that it happened at 1.30. However, I don't remember that the witness stated yesterday when the members came to her building. Or if the Prosecutor could indicate exactly in the record where the witness stated the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. 1.30 was not the time of the arrival of the 4th Detachment, and I don't believe that's what I said. I said, "the passage of the night from about 1.30 in the morning through to dawn." And the witness on the unofficial transcript indicated the time -- let me see -- at 1.30, about 1.30 in the morning, when she woke up. And that was at line 7 on page 84 of yesterday's transcript. And then she went on to describe during the night how there had been a number of telephone calls received and that special -- 4th Detachment and special units arrived and that it was then later, after these events had passed, that the 4th Detachment and special units arrived and Mr. Miroslav Tadic was at the entrance, was standing by her entranceway, and that is at page 90 of yesterday's unofficial transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My remark was that the witness said no where that in the early hours they came to her apartment building. That's what the question was. And on page 90, in the answer, it was said -- the question was whether she saw some of the defendants. The witness said, [In English] "I didn't know about it but later I had opportunity one of the defendants standing by my entrance."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have this clarified, if possible, or if the Prosecution could maybe change the question and reword it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the problem is the fact that the witness did say she woke up around 1.30 and then the events unfolded towards -- as dawn was breaking. And then just deal with that, Miss Reidy, with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I don't think that's a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you testified yesterday that at some stage, special units and sections of the 4th Detachment arrived towards your building. Could you tell us about what time it was when these special forces and the 4th Detachment came to the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can answer this question. This happened in the early hours before noon. I could never -- I never knew the exact time and I don't think I could give you the exact time now because I didn't consult my watch, but it felt like an eternity.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you also testified yesterday that you then had the opportunity to see Mr. Miroslav Tadic standing at your entranceway. Could you tell us, to the best of your recollection, what time this was, when you saw Mr. Tadic standing at the entranceway to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that they had already started, the night was over, it was already visible, but I could not give you the exact hour. The only thing I can say is that it was early and it was before noon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So can I clarify, you said that the 4th Detachment and the special units arrived sometime in the morning before noon - you can't be very specific - and I understand you to say that you saw Miroslav Tadic in your entranceway at the same time. Did these incidents coincide more or less, the arrival of the 4th Detachment and the special units, and then your subsequent sighting of Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you now to look at the diagram in front of you on your screen? And it's P68 ID for the record. Yesterday you marked with an "A" where your apartment block is. On the diagram, there are a number of arrows - we will start with the left-hand street - a number of arrows drawn on which you instructed to be drawn. Could you please explain to the Court what the arrows on the left-hand street represent?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain this. These arrows represent the direction of the movement of the 4th Detachment, that is to say, of the first soldiers that I saw in my entire life.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the Witness use the pointer to show us which arrows she's talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, can I ask you to take the pointer and show us where you said you've seen -- you saw the first movements of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment members were passing by this street. They were moving slowly in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me -- the movement you saw on the street, you've indicated. Was that soldiers on foot, were they in vehicles or was it a mixture of vehicles and foot soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a mixture. In this direction, there was an armoured vehicle moving, and on the side of the vehicle and in front of the vehicle, there were pedestrians, people on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And people on foot, these were -- were these people on foot armed and wearing camouflage or military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had full weapons on them and they wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do see there is a building, in fact, just where you have the pointer on, a building with lots of entrances? Could you just explain to the Chamber what that building is? It's a building in front of 62 Edvard Kardelj.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building in front, I think you're referring to this one here, is a set of garages and they have entrances from this and this side.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And in front of the garages is indicated at the end of the arrows what I understand is to be a -- I believe it to be the -- an armoured vehicle, where an armoured vehicle stopped; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you witness all these movements from your apartment on the second floor, the third level, of 62 Edvard Kardelj?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is that the only armoured vehicle that stopped in front of your house that morning, or the only one that you could see from your font window?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this one vehicle, and that was quite enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you also, for the record, explain what is represented by the arrows on the right-hand side that come in from Edvard Kardelj Street, the two arrows which from the right-hand side then that pass down by entrances 7, 6 and 5 of your apartment complex?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. The first arrow indicates the entrance, the main entrance, into our building area. The second arrow indicates the pathway that leads to all the entrances into the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you see any movement of soldiers or other persons that morning of the 17th of April in around the area where you just indicated where the arrows are on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not notice it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So all the activity came from the left-hand side of your apartment building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. When --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a question, just a small question. The street where the arrows are on the left-hand side, what's the name of that street? On the right-hand side, you had Edvard Kardelj Street, but where you saw the movement of the 4th Detachment and the armed vehicle, what's the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this very moment, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you've told the Chamber that from your front living-room, you observed this movement of 4th Detachment and the armoured vehicle coming to park in front of the garages belonging to your apartment complex. Could you tell the Chamber what happened after the armoured vehicle came to a stop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, before the witness answers that question, I would like to know how high, how tall, the garage building is, because looking at the map, it would seem that the garage building and the witness's apartment building -- well, the garage building could well obscure the street, the no-name street. I want to know how tall the garage building is, and in relation to the witness's apartment building, from her window, could she see over the top of the garage building.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I think Her Honour's questions are clear. Could you explain the relation -- the height of your building compared to the garage and the view, obstructed or otherwise, you would have had from your front living-room window?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building that we are talking about, that is located here, is a prefabricated building and it consists of a larger number of prefabricated garages, and its height is no where more than 2 metres. The building does not have a roof. It has a flat ceiling. I lived on the second floor. I wouldn't be able to tell you what height my floor is on, but I had visibility of this entire area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now, Mrs. Kapetanovic, I had asked if you could tell the Chamber what happened immediately after the armoured vehicle you were watching came to stop in front of the garage building belonging to your apartment complex.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear commands, fast movements of soldiers could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What sort of commands could you hear? What --

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were very short, very strict. They were indicated direction of their movement and the entrances into which they were supposed to go in.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So were they commands telling the soldiers what action they should take? Is that the sort of command you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What did you do in -- what did you do when you saw this vehicle pulling up and then you heard the commands being given to soldiers and soldiers moving quickly? What was your reaction to this incident?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to wait for this moment as peacefully and as calmly as I could. I mean, I tried to wait for my encounter with the soldiers in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What were you are doing in your apartment at this time, as you said, to try to keep everything calm and peaceful, as you said?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to create an image of a spontaneous welcome. I took a bowl with eggs, as if I was going to make a cake for Easter. When I -- I gave my dog, Peggy, to my husband - then boyfriend - so that it would not look as if he had weapons in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So you tried to create an air of normality, is that it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly right, as if guests were arriving.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did members of these special units and 4th Detachment enter entrance number 2, the entrance to your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And how did you know that they had entered your entrance?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the noise that could be heard inside the entrance, in the hallways.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was this general noise or could you also hear instructions being shouted?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard instructions, commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall what the instructions were that you heard?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Open the door," and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you do when you could -- when you heard these instructions being shouted?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I opened the door, with my bowl in my hand, and I went downstairs and my husband went with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could I just for this introduction ask that the witness be shown P69 ID, which is the diagram that just depicts her apartment block? And it has an ERN of 02199072.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you just said that you came out of your apartment block -- or your apartment and you went downstairs. On the diagram in front of you, and using the pointer, could you just explain how far down the stairs you went when you heard the instructions to open the doors?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can show it. I came up to here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This is midway between the first and the second floor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's kind of a -- is it a landing area between the first and second floors?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a landing area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when you reached this point, what did you see or did you meet anybody when you got to this point?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On this landing, the first man I saw was Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Miroslav Tadic in civilian clothing or was he wearing a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had -- he was fully armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, you said that you saw Mr. Miroslav Tadic. Did you say anything to him or did he say anything to you on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I greeted him, and then he addressed me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me what I was doing there with this bowl and the eggs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you explain to him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told him I was making a cake for Easter.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you said your husband had also come out of your apartment block. Did Mr. Tadic address your husband or your then-boyfriend?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He addressed him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did he tell your boyfriend?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "You Major's son, you had better take your gun and fight and not hold that dog."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you explain what you understood Mr. Tadic to mean by first the comment to your husband, "Major's son," and secondly what he meant by, "You better take your gun and fight and not hold that dog"?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband was of military age and it was understood that he should fight.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did he mean by "Major's son"? Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. My husband's father, my then-boyfriend, was known by his nickname of "Major" and, therefore, my boyfriend was called "Major's son."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your husband react to this comment at all?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did react to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: " Weapons are not for me."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Tadic explain to you what was happening or give you any instructions as to what you should do after you'd had this initial interaction?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no explanation, and he entered my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he enter your apartment alone or did he enter with other -- did other men accompany him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not enter alone. He was accompanied.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: By approximately how many other people?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four, who entered my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the people who entered, were they also soldiers in military uniform and armed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were soldiers in camouflage uniforms and fully armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And after they'd entered your apartment, what did they proceed to do?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They began searching the entire apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they tell you what they were looking for?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They told me what they were looking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were looking for weapons and a radio transmitter.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did they find anything like that in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They found nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons or any radio transmitter in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had neither of the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After they'd finished searching and found nothing, did the soldiers, including Mr. Tadic, then leave your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very angry and they left the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was yours the only apartment they searched in that block or did they search the other apartments, too?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They searched also the other apartments in the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they find any weapons in any of the other apartments in the building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not find anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What was their reaction when they couldn't find any weapons?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were extremely angry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Tadic say anything to you after he couldn't find any weapons in the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you hear him say something to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you hear him say?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard him turning and speaking to Salko Porobic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you hear him say to Mr. Porobic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was asking Salko Porobic to show him the automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Porobic have an automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Salko had no weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And after Mr. Tadic had ask -- you overheard Mr. Tadic asking Mr. Porobic for the automatic rifle, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attempted to calm down Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could I ask you to look again at the diagram to your right? And if you could just point out where this particular interaction occurred, where Mr. Tadic was asking about the automatic weapon and he was getting angry and then you said you tried to calm him down?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I also ask, with the help of the usher, if you could just mark a "B" in that location where this interaction occurred?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, you said you tried to calm down Mr. Tadic. What did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Salko Porobic was a sick man and that he wasn't fit to carry arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you overhear Mr. Tadic giving instructions to any of the other soldiers who were accompanying him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- he will order that our floor be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he would order that or did you hear him give instructions to some of the men accompanying him, that they should destroy your floor?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was very angry that he would do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mrs. Kapetanovic, I don't quite understand that answer. It says -- the transcript says that you said, "He was very angry that he would do that." It's still not clear to me whether you overheard him give instructions to somebody else, saying that he would order your floor to be destroyed or he told you that he was going to order your floor to be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He didn't say that to me, but to his men.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we just go over this, please? What exactly did you hear him say to his men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said that the weapons must be found, and if it will not be found, then our floor will be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, just again, just to clear this up. We now know what Mr. Tadic allegedly said. But who did he say it to? Did he say it to his group of soldiers, "If you don't find weapons, destroy the floor"? Or did he make this general comment out loud that the floor will be destroyed, to anyone who was listening?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, if you could just clarify that for Her Honour.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I said that Mr. Miroslav Tadic was very angry because he did not find weapons, but he was sure that the weapons were here. And he said, in the presence -- our presence and presence of his men, that he will order that our floor be demolished, and it referred to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Let's make that clear. He said in your presence that he will order the floor to be demolished? He didn't as such give instructions to his men to demolish the floor if they didn't find the weapons?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, he did not order the floor to be demolished.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So this is clear, you heard him say to his men -- you heard him say to his men, "If we don't find the weapons, the floor will be destroyed"? That was the general comment more than an order to destroy the floor there and then, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, it was a comment, a comment, which lasted for quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After this comment, did the soldiers continue to search the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did they search everywhere in the apartment block, including the attic that you can see in the diagram?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were searching.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the soldiers find anything?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They found nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, as best as you can recall, can you tell us roughly how long this lasted, from the time that the men entered your apartment block, conducted searches of the flats and searched the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately almost two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Of the men who were in your apartment block, was it your impression that Miroslav was the one in charge of them?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And why do you say "absolutely"?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was the only one who was giving orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did the men follow his instructions?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The other men you've described who entered with him, could you tell whether they were locals, whether they were non-locals or whether there was a mixture of both locals and non-locals amongst the soldiers who entered your building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a mixture of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And how could you tell that there was some local and non-local? How could you distinguish between them?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only by their speech.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So some spoke with a typical local accent, and some spoke with what you testified yesterday to, an Ekavian or Serbian accent; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Miroslav Tadic himself, did you personally know any of the other soldiers who entered your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I couldn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When the soldiers had finished the searches and found nothing after you said about two hours, did they then leave your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They left our entrance, our section.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: They left your section. Did some soldiers remain around the apartment complex number 62 Edvard Kardelj?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they remained.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the armoured vehicle also remain or did the armoured vehicle move on to another location?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It remained here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder whether you could tell us whether you saw Mr. Tadic and these soldiers also go into number 1, number 3, number 4, Mr. Zaric's block, and so on, or was it just your entranceway and the block that you were living in that was searched in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the only entrance that such an operation was carried out when Mr. Tadic is in question. I'm speaking of that what I had seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just to follow up on that, it's quite clear that you only saw Mr. Tadic come into your apartment block. Could you tell, from what you could see or hear, whether or not soldiers had entered any of the other entrances?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the soldiers entered also the other entrances.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you tell this because you saw some of them going into the entrances or because you could hear orders being given for them to enter some of the other entranceways?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could hear the orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Then is that because you were then inside your block as the searching was going on, you couldn't see anything else outside during that period?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Witness, did you look out of your window? Could you see anything out of the window or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I did look through the window. A lot of commotion and quite a few soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was this before Mr. Tadic entered your building or after they had left?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After they had left.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Maybe I could just clarify that. You were looking out your window when you saw the armoured vehicle come down the street and pull up in front of your garage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they were arriving, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought that was cleared earlier on when she was describing how she saw them and pointed out to the arrows and all that. I don't see the reason for going over it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I just thought there may be an ambiguity on the record, but if it's clear to the bench, then that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You said that you looked out again after Mr. Tadic had left, and you said that the armoured vehicle stayed there. Did it stay there for the whole day or did it eventually leave from in front of your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did leave, but I do not recollect when.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did soldiers remain in and around your apartment complex after the armoured vehicle had left or did they leave with the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the soldiers remained.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: They remained guarding your building or what were they doing after the vehicle had left?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They remained there on guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were they on guard in front of your building, in front of particular entrances, or were they patrolling the streets and the area in which the building was?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were standing in front of the building, as well as along the streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask you to look at diagram P68 again, which indicates the apartment complex? And using the pointer, could you indicate where you could see some soldiers still standing after the armoured vehicle had left?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps I could just ask you to take a marker again and just mark those areas where you could see some soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate roughly how many soldiers you saw there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number but there were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you say "quite a few," would that be four or five or more than ten, or could you just give us some rough idea of how many were there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figure would be approximately around ten.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And you could see this from your windows of your apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, leave your apartment for the rest of that day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not leave the apartment at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Had you received any instruction not to leave your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Such instructions were issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you tell us who issued those instructions or how you were told that you shouldn't leave the apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear any direct instructions but people in the building informed me about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall now who informed you that there was such instructions?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Mr. Tubakovic, Mr. Djorde Tubakovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he ever tell you who had given him these instructions?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He never told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did some other people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness a question directly. Yesterday, you told us that Mr. Tubakovic is Serbian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So he was -- was he also confined to the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His apartment was not searched, and he could move around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did in fact, however, some families who were living in your apartment block, did they leave during that day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of that day, some apartments were abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was this because you'd received instructions that some women and children would be allowed to evacuate?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you tell me who left your apartment block that day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the following families left: family Porobic, family Culumovic, and two ladies, Avdibegovic and Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did the men -- were the men from these families able to leave as well or did the men return?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went with them but then they were returned, turned back.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The family Avdibegovic, I don't believe you mentioned before. Could you just confirm what ethnicity they are?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are Muslim -- of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you not try to leave when these families left?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only free route was towards Crkvina and into the internal parts, central parts of Bosnia, and I had no one there. I'm from Croatia, and that route was blocked and all I could do was wait.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, did that mean that you were the only non-Serb woman left in your apartment block by the end of the 17th April, by the night of the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mrs. Culumovic and the other ladies. I apologise, I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's no problem. I'll repeat it. You've testified that the Porobic, the Culumovic, the Avdibegovic and the Halilovic families tried to evacuate later in the afternoon and that the men had returned. And after this had happened, my question was: Did that mean that you were the only non-Serb female left in your apartment block, block 2, of number 62 Edvard Kardelj Street?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I'd just like to set a time frame for a moment. Could you tell me, at some stage after this takeover, were you detained?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was detained in my entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But were you at some stage taken away and detained at another building or complex?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Later, a month or so later, were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And just to give us the time frame, could you -- do you recall when this first arrest occurred?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it occurred on the 15th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. So from the 18th of April, when you were the only non-Serb woman in your apartment block, up until the 15th of May, when you said you were arrested, did you remain primarily in your apartment complex?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was exclusively and only in my entranceway.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You say exclusively in your entranceway. Did that mean you didn't try to leave the building and you didn't go into town or wander into any other areas of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't even try to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you ever approached to do forced labour during this period?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did your then boyfriend, now husband, remain with you throughout this period, April 18th to approximately May 15?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He remained with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did he at that stage have to do forced labour?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tried to avoid forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did he manage to avoid it at that time when you were together in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know why he managed to avoid the forced labour?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through his uncle.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you just explain how his uncle was able to prevent him being taken for forced labour in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His uncle sent non-Serbs, that is to say, he assigned non-Serbs to do work assignments, work obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Where was his uncle working?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, he worked at the military staff. During the war, his role was to assign forced labourers to their forced labour duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Whilst you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what ethnic background your then boyfriend's uncle was -- is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He comes from a typical Muslim family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And can I -- you said during the war that his role was to assign or to hand out -- to assign the forced labour tasks. Do you know where he was working when this was his assignment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was working at the local commune, and his -- he had such responsibilities starting on the 17th of April, but actually I'm not quite sure of the date. It was during the war in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did other people in your apartment block have to carry out forced labour assignments during this time?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All non-Serbs had to carry out forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you witness these people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do apologise for interfering in this examination. Sorry, my friend. Do we have instruction with regard to the terms used during the examination, such as "forced labour" or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we've had those instructions for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's possible because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I did say that we are using them generally because it seems to be easier, but then the Prosecution know what they have to prove --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- on forced labour. We have been through that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because it's, you know, a little bit confusing here. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, the question I'd asked was -- you testified that other non-Serbs in the building had to do forced labour, and I'm just going to ask you: Did you witness them leaving to do forced labour and coming home? Is that how you know that they had to do forced labour?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how I knew. I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also hear of any other changes in the period April 18 to May 15? And now I'm speaking of the restrictions that were imposed upon the non-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What sort of restrictions had you heard had been imposed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Restriction of movement, no more than two Muslims were allowed together. Also, people had to be marked with armbands. Doors had to be marked, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, you said that no more than two Muslims were allowed together. This also applied to persons of Croat nationality or was it just for Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It referred to all those who were not Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You also said that people had to be marked with armbands. Was this non-Serb persons had to wear arm bands?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you said that doors had to be marked and so on. Was this that doors belonging to, again, non -- the non-Serb population should be marked to identify them? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall now what was used to mark the apartment doors?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name "Slobodan Stanisic" was taken off of my apartment door because the apartment was no longer a Serb apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you mean that the names of all non-Serbs were taken -- from what you could see, they took away names of non-Serbs from their apartment doors?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall now how you heard that these restrictions had been imposed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the order personally but I was told about it in the entranceway.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when you said you were told about it in the entranceway, who told you about it in the entranceway?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tenants that had remained.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So is this some of the other tenants who were indeed out in public and that they came back and told you of these new restrictions in town? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, whilst you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you just mention the name of which tenants in your block told you this, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Culumovic and Mr. Tubakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, whilst you were in your apartment block during this approximate month period, did you ever get any further visits from soldiers or members of the special units?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Daily.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And could you tell us in which period this happened? Did this happen in the beginning -- in the initial period from the 18th of April, in around the 18th of April, or did it happen later on, shortly before you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened from the very beginning, and it happened always at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So it happened from the 18th. Could you tell us exactly what happened? You said it happened always at the same time. What time did these visits occur?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. They would come exclusively during lunchtime every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who would come? How many -- well, do you know the people who would come to your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never seen them before, but I know there was one woman escorted by four members of the special units, and they called themselves extraordinary specialists. They had camouflage uniforms on and they were fully armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what would happen when they came to your apartment in around lunchtime every day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The woman, or actually this young woman, would put her pistol against my head while others were searching my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they tell you what at the were looking for when they searched your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what were they looking for?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were looking for the radio transmitter and for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did they ever find any radio transmitters or weapons?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- no, they never found anything in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have any radio transmitters or weapons in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd never had any weapons. I hate weapons. I had a very small radio transmitter but its range was only two rooms, so that if you were in one room you could hear it in the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they ever find that and take it away?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder whether we could clarify the use of this term "radio transmitter," because I think we have had it used in terms of the soldiers, on all of these occasions they came to the apartment were looking for weapons and a radio transmitter. Now, Mrs. Kapetanovic, you mention that you had a small radio transmitter that was in one room and you could hear it from potentially another room, but you used the word "radio transmitter" again. Are you referring in that context, the second context, to an ordinary radio that you listened to broadcasts on or are you referring to a transmitter where you receive messages and you send messages? So if you could just clarify what you mean in the context of you had a small radio transmitter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will gladly do so. I was always asked to show radio transmitters or to show them that I had radio transmitters that professionals were using, and what I had, I used to communicate with my husband if we happened to be in the next room. It was more like a toy for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But Mrs. Kapetanovic, could you just again explain a radio transmitter, by that you mean some form of walkie-talkie or Motorola radio where you would talk to each other through these radios? Is that you mean by a radio transmitter?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean by this is the complete equipment, including the radio, with its frequencies, and a walkie-talkie, that was used for communicating. That is a radio transmitter, this whole equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And this small radio transmitter you said that you did have which you used for communicating between rooms, was that ever found and taken away by any of these special units who came to search your house?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed it to them immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you show it to the soldiers who were with Miroslav Tadic on the first day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what was their reaction when they saw it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were interested in it. It was a toy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes the witness said, "They were not interested in it. It was a toy."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think, Mrs. Kapetanovic, that was just a clarification for the record. So on each occasion that -- so on the first occasion, on the 17th, when you had been searched by soldiers accompanying Mr. Miroslav Tadic and on the proceeding occasions where you had these daily lunchtime searches by members of the special forces, they knew that you had this small, baby radio transmitter and they were not interested in that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They immediately received this toy from me, but they were not interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you alone in your apartment when these people came to search or were there other people there when they conducted these searches?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was happening at lunchtime and I was not alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who else was with you when this was going on?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the men from my entranceway were there, who had remained. I was the only non-Serb woman who could prepare at least one cooked meal for them. So they all gathered in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So these special forces would come in when everybody was there and conduct these searches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did this continue every day until you were arrested or was it only for a short period of time, a week or so?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was happening for a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long these searches continued for?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe around ten days.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to take you to the 15th or so of May, which was the day you testified you were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a question. I'll go back to the events on the 17th of April and the first search of your apartment, when Mr. Tadic entered your entrance, and you said that you had gone down from your apartment and that then Mr. Tadic addressed you and your boyfriend, and your boyfriend, I'm not -- I don't have the help of the transcript, but if my memory serves me right, he addressed you, and you said that Mr. Tadic said to your boyfriend, "You'd better leave that dog, take your weapon and fight." How did you understand -- did you understand that it was seriously meant and how did you understand that comment or statement by Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me, this was a very serious remark. Weapons are not a joke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: No, but how did you understand it? Against whom would he be fighting? If Mr. Tadic seriously meant what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I just understood what your question was about. He was supposed to fight with them. That's what he meant, because he addressed him, and it would be logical to conclude that my husband should go with Mr. Tadic to fight for his town. That's what it looked like to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Kapetanovic, I said -- if I can ask you to focus on the events around the 15th or so of May, which you've testified was the day of your arrest. Were you in your own apartment on the 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you get a visit that day from any soldiers and members of the special units?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, soldiers came to my apartment. I don't know if they might have also been members of the special police. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How many persons came to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two entered my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And could you tell us roughly what time of the day it was? Was it the morning, afternoon, late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime around noon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did the soldiers want when they entered your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They entered it and one of them asked to see my ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you show him your ID?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did the soldier do after he'd read your identification card?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He returned the ID to me and he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What name was on your identification card at this time? This would be mid-May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It said, and I was very lucky that it said, "Jelena Stanisic, Edvard Kardelj, S62, Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you say you were very lucky, why is that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Jelena can also be a Serb name, and my last name, Stanisic, is a typical Serb last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So do you think the soldier thought that you were a Serb when he read your name?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he knew very well who I was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you explain that? Did you know this soldier who was looking at your identification card?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised him later. I was lucky that he also recognised me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who was he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my late husband's best man.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: He was my late husband's best man's son.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So do I understand that the soldier who was your late husband's, I'll call him godson, although he knew that you were Croat, he pretended for the sake of the other soldiers who were with him that you were a Serb and he left you alone? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Miss Reidy, just for the sake of clarity, there is a difference between a best man - and I think the word in B/C/S is "kum" - we've heard it before, and what you now termed a godson. Somebody's godson, where you attend the baptism and you're the godmother or the godfather, that is a different person. So just for clarity's sake, maybe you could rephrase it. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. Just for the record, I think the interpreter corrected it and said that the person who came was her late husband's best man's son, so not the best man, but Your Honour, I'll use that phrase in the future rather than godson. I had been led to believe it was more or less interchangeable.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, maybe you could help us with that. The soldier, you said was the son of your late husband's best man. Does that mean that he was the son of your husband's friend who was a witness at his wedding or that also your husband had a particular role, kind of a protective role, to play over that soldier, over his Kum's son?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Godfather.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father-in-law held this child at his baptismal ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So your husband was the godfather of this soldier who came to see you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour, for the correct word.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'll ask one or two more questions before the break. After this soldier left, did -- was that the end of the events for the day, or did more soldiers come to visit you later that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding is that in fact this young man was a godfather's son, and here in the transcript, I don't see this connection. In fact, it was page 35, line 9, the witness said, "My father-in-law held this child at his baptism ceremony." And, of course, her father-in-law was a godfather to this young soldier. That's the relation. It's not so clear here. Maybe I'm wrong. I allow this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. We are taking a lot of time on this. My understanding was that this young soldier was the son of the man who was best man at the late -- at the wedding of the witness with her late husband. Is that correct, Mrs. Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was there at the christening. He was the godson.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But her father-in-law was a godfather to this young soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To the soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So it's not directly related with the -- his or her father. It's a father-in-law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Father-in-law, yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the clarification, but we know about which relation we are speaking about, as a matter of clarity. I don't know if it helps for our friend from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's, frankly, the soldier who came knew who she was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's sufficient. Can we have our break? It's 10.30. We will resume our proceedings at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Miss Reidy, examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I'd like now to focus on the events of the afternoon of the 15th or so of May, 1992, after the first visit to your apartment by some Serb soldiers. Did you receive a second visit later that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there was this visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did soldiers come to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They entered my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did they say to you when they entered your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I am being arrested, that I must go downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they tell you why you were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not tell me why I was being arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did they tell you where they were going to take you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that precise moment, they didn't tell me where they -- where I'll be going.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the people who came to your apartment, were they in military uniform and armed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they permit to you take any personal belongings with you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that I can take something with me, but I didn't know at the time what I would be needing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So did you leave the apartment then in just what you had on you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When they took you out of your apartment and downstairs, what happened to you then?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of my entrance, a truck was parked without the roof, the tarpaulin was raised, and police were standing by it or, rather, people in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the people in uniform, did it look to you like they were in police uniform or more of a military, soldier-style uniform?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And were you required to get into the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They told me to get into the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were there already some people in the truck when you climbed aboard?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some people were already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people who were already inside the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I knew them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who were these people in the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was this family, I believe that their surname was Kljajic, Anto, his wife, their son Miro, and their daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnicity of this family?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What ethnicity was the family?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are Croats, Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you climbed aboard the truck, where did the truck go to next?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went into the first road, on the left, towards -- directed towards a house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have minor question here. What kind of truck are we talking about? You are using, "getting into the truck," and "get aboard the truck." Was it an open truck or what kind of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can explain it. That truck -- well, I'll never forget it in my life. It wasn't a very big truck, with a tarpaulin which only at the back end was opened. And within the truck, there was no flooring, only benches on the sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do I understand you to say that you got into the back of the truck, which is open, covered by a tarpaulin, and the family Kljajic you've told us about were sitting on the benches, on the side of the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And so were you all under the tarpaulin in the back of the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you'd left -- you described the vehicle leaving your apartment block and it went towards another house. Whose house did it go towards?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stopped in front of the house -- allow me to remember -- Ruza Matic. But at this point, I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I believe her name was Ruza Matic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know this woman who was in the house, even if you're not sure of her name now?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Of what ethnic background is she, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know. She was -- she is Croat and a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When they stopped in front of her house, was she required to join you in the back of the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was she alone or did she have any of her children with her -- or any children with her?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was with her young boy, her son.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these the last passengers you picked up or did the truck continue to collect other people?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, we were the only ones there on that truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where did that truck take the seven or eight of you who were aboard?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the area in proximity of the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did it stop near the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It stopped at a police checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did anything happen at this police checkpoint? Was anybody taken off the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It did happen. They were removed from the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who exactly were removed from the truck, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kljajic and his son.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to where they were taken?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what information did you have about their destination?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they are being taken to the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you learn that they ended up in the secondary school later?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you recall now how you learnt they'd been taken to the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- from the wife of Mr. Kljajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. After this checkpoint and when the two men were removed, where did the truck continue on to?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truck continued in a direction which was unknown to me, and we couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was that because you were under the tarpaulin you couldn't see exactly which -- along which route you were being taken? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where did the truck finally stop? Where was your final destination in the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truck stopped at the checkpoint in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Crkvina is a village or an area outside of Bosanski Samac town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is in evidence a number of maps with Crkvina marked on it so I don't intend to go through it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you stopped at this checkpoint at Crkvina what happened? Were you required to get off the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where were you taken after you dismounted from the truck?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the stadium in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you say a stadium, do you mean a sports stadium?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a football ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps at this point I could introduce the third diagram which the witness gave instructions to draw up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It is a diagram with the ERN number 02199071, and it's my understanding that the Bench were distributed their copies yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, do you recognise the diagram which is on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is it a rough diagram of the sports stadium to which you said you were taken to in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And it was drawn up following your instructions of the layout of the place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
