utterances.text: Perhaps, can I ask you to take the pointer and just point to the shaded block on the right-hand corner with the "P" marked on it? Is that where the checkpoint was, which you first said you stopped at?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That was the first checkpoint in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you then tell me where exactly, from the truck, you were taken to it and where you had to dismount from the trucks?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And that you -- is that the entrance to the sports field?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the big darkened area there on your left, that is an open air sports pitch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you dismounted from the trucks, what could you see in the sports field? Was it empty or were there already a lot of people there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many, many people.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you have a rough idea of how many people might have been there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few hundred.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you recognise any of these people or did you get to know who these people were or what ethnicity the people were, more precisely?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I managed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you tell us what ethnicity the people gathered in that sports stadium were?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few Muslim women, and the rest, Croats of Catholic faith.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And these Muslim women, were they, to the best of your knowledge, mainly Muslim women married to Catholic -- married to Croat men?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And were there just women there or were there women, children and men gathered in this stadium?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Children, women, men, old people of all ages, of all ages.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps I could just get this document now marked for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P70 ID, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, did you -- a few hundred of you who were gathered there, did you spend the rest of that day outside in the air, in the field of that sports stadium?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you find anybody that you recognised amongst the hundreds gathered there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did recognise.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you find any of your relatives there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My aunt, Mariska.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. During the time that you were -- you and all the others were kept in this field, did anybody, any soldiers, ever approach the people gathered there and take personal belongings from them?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who was taking things away from the detainees?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what sort of things were they taking from the detainees?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything they had with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Documents, or was it primarily jewellery and perhaps what you could call items of value?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All items of value: Gold, money, watches, exclusively items of value.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did this happen to everybody who was gathered or was it mainly people gathered around the entrance to the stadium?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were the closest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. When you say, Mrs. Kapetanovic, that what was taken was exclusively items of value, in the list you gave of gold, money, watches, you didn't say one way or the other about ID, identification documents, which Ms. Reidy had also asked you. Could you answer directly on that point? Was your documentation also taken away or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents were taken from us at the first checkpoint at Samac, near the school, so that those who arrived there didn't have documents on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have your identification documents with you when you left the house?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I had nothing on me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So I take it, then, they couldn't have removed your identification document basically from the fact that you didn't have one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, not this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you spend the evening in the field or did you get to enter or did you go inside to spend the night?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the night, the door was opened and we were allowed to enter into this building called the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could again be shown P70 ID and she could explain what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 46, line 3, I think it's a kind of mistake in transcript. Now it's P70, because there is a P730 ID, but it's corrected now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's P70 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's 730 number of the exhibit, which is actually P70. Now it's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could you explain where you were taken on the evening of the day that you were detained in this sports stadium? Explain where they brought you in to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We entered through this door and the majority went in that direction, and they settled in this area which I am now showing. Women and small children went on the podium, and due to the big crowd, I -- the crowdedness, I went into a smaller area, something like a locker room or something similar, and I settled there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: There is an "X" on that diagram. Is that where you took up your position to spend the night?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a very small space between the door and the wall. And when the door is opened, then I remained in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you go there by yourself or were you there with your aunt who you had located in the football pitch earlier, the sports pitch earlier?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- yes. More than one of us, a few of us, entered there, and it included my aunt.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you provided with anything to sleep on, a mattress or blankets or anything?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I found a piece of cardboard.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a question. If we look at this picture, are these darkened squares, are they open places or are they buildings? These two, "bina" stage and the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain it to you. This square represents a wooden podium where the actors would have their performances, and all of this represented an auditorium, an entirety, and this area, from that side is closed and represents -- and this place represents another part of the building which is within the building itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: A further question: So this square in totality, this with dark parts and light parts, that's a building, a covered building with roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So the crowd gathered in the sport field was transferred into the entirety of this building in different parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only in the area which I will mark for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: And it's a question of several hundred peoples gathered within this space?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, can we have some marking by the witness to show the areas of the building where people -- the parts which were occupied by the people from the stadium? Because it appears there is one part where people were not moved to.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, perhaps you could take that red marker that's -- I believe it's with you on the ELMO, and could you again just outline, with the red marker, the part of the building where you could all try to find somewhere to rest that evening?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. The places marked with "X" and this red line are the location where several hundred prisoners moved around and lived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I have a question as to the amount of people. Just to get this clear, Mrs. Kapetanovic, initially you responded to Ms. Reidy on page 43, line 13, when she asked you to give us a rough idea of how many people there might have been, your response was, "a few hundred," but now, in response to Judge Lindholm's question, where he said to you, "It's a question of several hundred people," and you said, "Precisely so." Now, at least in the English language, there is a difference between "few" and "several." I wonder if you could clarify it by saying there were approximately, you know, 200, 300, whatever it was, so that we have a sort of visualisation of it, if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. At any rate, there was more than 300 people at the moment when we entered this enclosed area. At the moment when we entered it, that's how many people were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And perhaps just to clarify, you said that's how many there were when you entered. Did other people join you in the stadium after you had entered it? So did the number of people in the stadium increase by the time you'd entered the centre at night?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the time, more people were arriving.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So again, just in the manner that Her Honour Judge Williams asked, by the time you went into the sports and cultural centre, roughly how many of you could you guess were trying to fit into that space?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were crammed in like sardines, and up to 500 people could be crammed in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that why you tried to find a little place behind the door, because it was the only place you could find some room?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crowd was huge, and the normal way led to the big hall. I went right into the first room on the right, together with my aunt and some other persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was that to avoid everybody squashing into the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, I think we have had enough of an explanation of how the people were crammed into the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, during that day, had you received any food?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We received a slice of bread and a little piece of bacon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And had you had access to water during the day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was worried about water on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But was any water distributed to you, if you'd wanted to have something to drink?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no water on the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have access to a toilet?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We found one toilet.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would you just again take the pointer and indicate on the map where that single toilet was?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's a place in the diagram where a "T" is marked, is that it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And is that -- that's a toilet for one person, is it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an outside toilet for just one person.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And that was the only toilet available to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not enough. We also used the areas that I will indicate right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could just take again the pen and mark a "T" number "2" or something, just where you've marked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think "T2" will do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But we need an explanation on T2. Was it an open area? Was it a small building? Because the other "T" was actually a toilet.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll pursue that right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I think you can understand that we need some clarification. First, just could you tell me, this place you've marked, was it an actual toilet or was it a makeshift area that you designated for use as a toilet?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have to explain at this moment is not very nice, but I will try to be very mild. This was an area, it was not closed, this was an area where garbage was left, and there was a lot of human feces. There were many things there that were not very nice, and we had to go and squat there, more people at a time. I apologise to Your Honours, but that's simply what the truth is. I would also like to add that a guard was also present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder whether you could just give one further explanation. Where you've indicated the T2, was that area being used when you were contained in the soccer field? And were you, therefore, let out of the soccer field with a guard to go to the T2 place? And then I have another question, which is: When you were in the building, the sports centre, for the night, were there other toilet facilities inside the building for use during the night-time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer as follows. In the building itself or in the area that we were allowed to use, there were no toilet facilities. During the day, we had the right to access both toilet 1 and toilet 2. During the night, it didn't even occur to the craziest person that they should go to any of the toilet facilities. People relieved themselves where they were lying. I do apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is no need to apologise, Mrs. Kapetanovic. This evidence is important for this case because the Trial Chamber would like to know how such a large crowd of people were looked after wherever they were detained. So it is important that you give these details.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, just one more question on this subject. This area designated for use as a toilet, what you've marked now on the map as T2, was that available from the very first day when you were brought into the stadium or was this an area designated in the days that followed your initial detention or was it set up -- was it already there when you were brought in?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day, I didn't use any toilet facilities. I think that nobody else used them either, out of fear. We were just sitting wherever we found ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And so do I understand that the second area you designated for use of toilet after it became clear that the regular outdoor toilet was not going to be sufficient to cope with the numbers of people who were being detained? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a question. Just a question of -- about hygiene. When using toilet 1, which was a real toilet, were you supplied with toilet paper or anything like that? And Question No. 2: When using what you call toilet 2, although it was no toilet, were you supplied with any kind of tissues or toilet paper or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What -- I would like you to imagine what I'm going to tell you. This, I'm referring to the toilet number 1 now. This was a very small room made of brick and there was a hole in the ground. It was a type of latrine. And two planks that used to be a door could not obscure the entire view of the toilet, so if somebody entered the toilet, these people sitting on this entire area here could see the person in the toilet. When you were standing, when you were trying to stand between this hole, there was really no where you could stand, and you can imagine what our feet looked like. Your Honour, there was no such thing as toilet paper there. There was not even enough drinking water, let alone toilet paper, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I'd like now to continue with what happened after all the detainees were moved inside to the centre. You've already explained where you spent the night. Did anything happen during that first night or was it uneventful?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we all entered the room, all the doors behind us were closed. The centre had no electricity so we found ourselves in pitch darkness. During the night, I can't exactly remember when exactly it was at this moment, but you could hear women crying; you could hear noise and shoutings. It was very, very unpleasant to hear all these things. A lot of stuff happened during this night.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was there something in particular that caused these women to cry or that caused this particular shouting?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. What was going on in the big room, which I'm going to indicate to you right now, was not unknown to us, but I do know with certainty what was going on in my room. Armed people came and they had a flashlight, and they were asking for men. The only man who was in the small room was the son, I think he was ten years old, the son of Mrs. Ruza Matic. They wanted to take him away from his mother and she started to cry, and she said that he was still just a boy, a child. After a lot of discussion, they left the child and left. That's what I saw that night.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any other men in the room that you had chosen to sleep in?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the room that I slept in, there were no other men, but in the larger room, yes, there were other men there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to the men in the larger room that night?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this large room, only women, children and some very old people remained. All the men had been taken away into an unknown direction. Furthermore, the men that were being taken out of the rooms were beaten. That's what their wives said.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me -- their wives told you that they had been beaten. Do you know if they were beaten in front of their wives and children as they were taken away or could they hear shouts or sounds of people being beaten once the men had been removed from the area of detention?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were beaten right by the entrance. They were lined up and beaten there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could again just assist us by showing us on the diagram where you were told the men were lined up and beaten.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. This is the entrance through which they would be taken out. This is where they were lined up and then driven away.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps just for the record, you could take a -- another marker, another colour marker, perhaps the green one or the blue one - that's fine - and just mark it with a "Y" perhaps where they were -- an arrow, to indicate where they were lined up.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as you were in the other room, you testified that you couldn't see what was going on but you could hear all this noise and commotion that night, could you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. You could hear it from a great distance. It was that loud.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So in the morning, when you woke up, I take it there were just women and children and some elderly persons left?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you spend that second day inside the centre or were you again taken out into the field?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have a question here. Ms. Reidy, you spoke about "woke up in the morning." Did you sleep at all during that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that night, nobody slept.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When morning arrived, then, is probably a better way of phrasing my question, what happened? Did you -- were you taken out again or did you leave the room that you'd been sleeping in and go into the larger room, or how did you find out what had happened in the other room?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it dawned, we could see, first of all, where we were, and second of all, I had the opportunity to enter the larger room. There I heard from the women who had spent the night there what had happened there. We were allowed to move around this room.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you stay inside during the day or were you again taken out to the field?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hours before noon, the guards came and opened the door. I'm going to indicate which door. This door here. And they let us go to the football field again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps again, just so we have clarity of the record, if there is a smaller pen there, you could put a number 1 beside that entrance which is the entrance you used to go in and out of the sports pitch.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. During the second day, were you kept -- did you spend the whole day of the second day in the sports field?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We spent the whole day in this field.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you receive food?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, during the afternoon, they brought us a slice of bread and a little piece of bacon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they provide you with drinking water?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They allowed us -- actually, they allowed some women to go fetch water but they were -- they had guards going with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again on the diagram, could you just point out to us where the women went to collect the water from?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's the circle with the "W" in it, is it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And it's a well from which they collect water; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So they would go with armed guard, collect some water and bring it back to the people in the stadium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: With the men removed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Reidy. Still on this same question or issue of food and drink, you had mentioned that there were babies and young children, including the 7 year old boy. Were the children given anything extra or was their ration the same as for the adult persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was nothing extra for them, only bread and bacon was unloaded, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I'm just going to ask if you could give us some idea of numbers, how many people were now left, since the men had been taken away the night before.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were a little bit under 300 persons there. That's what I found out later.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'll come to how she found out the numbers later when we arrive at that chronologically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I take it on this day, did you begin to use the makeshift toilet, the place you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is the usher still required, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think that for the moment, the usher can sit down. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you did testify that in the first day people were scared and didn't want to go to the -- go to any of the toilet facilities, but on the second day, is this when you began also to use this designated area of a makeshift toilet, the place you marked as T2?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We simply had to go somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I think you said you were always accompanied by a guard when you went; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were the people guarding you armed guards, or the people armed guarding you in the stadium throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will show their direction of their movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would Your Honours like that marked for the record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I mean, simply describing that they were moving all around the area of the pitch and the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think the record can reflect that there were soldiers all around the circumference of the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The second night, did you also spend that inside, in the centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the evening, again, the doors were opened, and now everybody took his own -- occupied his own place.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: By this time, had anyone told you, given you an explanation as to you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was the second night in the sports centre, was it a relatively peaceful night?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Then on the third day, I understand that something happened. Could you tell us, on the third day, did you decide to react to the conditions in which you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the third day, I decided to do something, not only for myself but for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So could you explain the third day, was this in the morning of the third day or later on, on the third day? When did you decide that perhaps the time had come to do something?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning hours, before leaving the area, before going to the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I'm going to get to what action you took, but what made you decide that you were going to do something?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, do understand how we -- what the stench was coming from us after only three days. People were becoming -- getting sick. It was -- the situation with the children was critical, and we were asking ourselves why were we here and how long shall we be there, and what our fate will be? And everybody had practically the same questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just to confirm, by the third day, already some of the children amongst you were sick?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So what did you decide to do on the morning of the third day that you'd been detained?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I availed myself of the fact that the guards were in the big room. I stood -- placed on a big desk, a smaller one and a chair. Then I banged with my foot, and I asked everybody for a bit of attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could you -- a lot of information -- perhaps first on the diagram, you could just show us where you had these tables placed upon which you stood?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have the pen accessible to you, could you just put a 2 on that location?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. So you had put up this makeshift platform for yourself. Did any of the guards try to stop you when you assembled this?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a total shock. They were just looking, staring at me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So what happened after you asked for silence?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I'm addressing all detainees and that I beg them to follow my instructions, instructions which consisted of the following: Firstly, that every person should attempt to clean the area where he was -- the person was living. Secondly, that no one should speak to the guards or those who enter at night. I also asked them for total discipline. And I asked the guards to bring us someone with whom we could talk, negotiate. I asked for the Red Cross, the local Red Cross, the International Red Cross. I asked for the then-representatives of the UNPROFOR. I asked for somebody who -- the person who was standing behind the order and who signed the order for our arrest.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you said you asked the guards to bring someone you could talk with and for various representatives, what was the reaction of the guards?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were shocked and went out.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did all of them leave or did just one or two of the guards leave the room?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Guards remained at certain points within this big hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the guards bring you someone to talk with, that you had requested -- as you'd requested?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After some time elapsed, and they brought in people into this big hall where -- which I did not leave, and these were the following: the representative of the Red Cross, for whom I believe was from Crkvina, and also Mr. Ranko Popovic, who addressed me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: To clarify, this person from the Red Cross you believe was from Crkvina, I take it to mean it was from a local Red Cross branch, not the International Red Cross from Geneva?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so, the representative of the local Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you said that Mr. Ranko Popovic addressed you. Is Mr. Ranko Popovic a civilian or was he a soldier, or who was he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in uniform, and the other gentleman was in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Popovic armed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now what exactly did Mr. Popovic say to you when he was brought into this big room?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me that he cannot bring in anyone of those representatives that I requested. He also told me that we were there due to war circumstances, and that he didn't know how long we would be staying there. It all depended on the war in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you -- were you given any idea what position Mr. Popovic held so that he was the one who was able to give you this information?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, he did not represent his function but he was a superior, that is how others who turned to him. Obviously, he had a function in these closed premises which I term as a camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. After Mr. Popovic had told you that you'd been detained because of the war circumstances and he didn't know how long you'd be detained, did you ask him to provide you with any other facilities?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I told him that we have problems with the small children, that we have also some very sick old people, who were bedridden. I asked for any type of food so that we'd be able to feed all who were present there. I also begged that we be allowed to have the toilet cleaned - and I'm referring to T1 - and that we be allowed any type of cooking whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what was the response to these requests?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He answered that he would see what he could do, and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You mentioned that you told him that you had some sick old people and children?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, do not repeat. Just go ahead and ask the next question for whatever happened next.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Did any medical people come to the centre to see these sick people and sick children?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, what did the person from the Red Cross do? You mentioned he came in but you didn't mention what he actually did. Did he speak to people? Did he -- well, in any event, maybe you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. He was a civilian who listened to this dialogue between me and Mr. Popovic, and together with Mr. Popovic, he exited, he left. They said that they would see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a further question, a follow-up question. Did the representative of the local Red Cross inspect the premises and the conditions there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was standing at the door where we were having this discussion. I can show you the location on this diagram. He was standing inside, close to the door, without any movement along this hall or around it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So he didn't inspect the toilet 1 and the so-called toilet 2, or any other places in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never. No one ever inspected anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you receive any further food after Mr. Popovic and the representative of the Red Cross had left?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, the representatives of the Red Cross did bring in, on a temporary basis, a big pot in which we could cook.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This was just a simple pot, was it? Not a stove or something? Just a plain, ordinary pot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the first moment, at the improvised toilet number 2, we found some old bricks which we placed one on top of another. On that, we placed the pot, poured some water. And we were lucky to find a chicken which was brought in by a detainee who was arrested while he was going to the market. So we slaughtered this hen and we placed it in the pot to cook it. As we were there already three days, I went to check the area around the goal gate, and I found two eggs, and it was this, my first strange lunch that I had as a detainee. What we received, we distributed for the -- gave it to the children, but regrettably, they all acquired diarrhoea from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one thing: So the Red Cross -- if I understand correctly, the Red Cross provided a cooking pot but they didn't provide any food to be cooked. You had to -- you were just lucky that the man had the chicken and you found the eggs. So for almost 300 people, there was a pot but no food, is that -- food to cook? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Unfortunately, it was precisely so. The small amount of food went for the children. After they saw that I persisted and that I would demanding more for these poor people, they allowed to bring in a stove with a very big pot, and on that day, they brought in also some food in order to cook for those who would be then lucky enough to have something to eat. I don't know how I could conjure it up for you, this culinary specialty and my culinary abilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And just one last thing concerning that answer. You mentioned "they" allowed a stove to be brought in, and also "they" brought in some food. Who is the "they"? Is the "they" the guards and Mr. Popovic? And also, who brought the food in? Was that the Red Cross or was it somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About all this which was brought in was brought in by the guards on this -- and Ranko Popovic and the man from the Red Cross saw to it that it was brought in. I had to sign, when the pots were being handed to us, I had to sign a receipt for this inventory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could you just turn to the diagram again, P70? It's still on the right on the ELMO. And could you just point out to us where you set up this temporary cooking area?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That circle marked with a "K" is where you had set up this makeshift kitchen?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You've explained -- did you also request that some of the women who were detained be allowed back to their villages to take whatever food they had and bring it back to the sports centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the shortage of foodstuff, I thought that this was the only logical solution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was that permitted?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did armed guards take the women to their villages and bring them back?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a truck, they took the women from Hasici, from Tisina and from Zasavica. They took them to their villages and, under guard, they were then returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was the food you had available to you then, the chicken and eggs, this food which the women had brought back, was this the only food available to you or had the Red Cross brought extra food?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most important item was the milk for the children. Women succeeded in milking the cows and to bring it back.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So the women who had been taken to the villages were able to bring back some milk for the children; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross deliver foodstuffs to you beyond the pots you've already described or was your food source, just your food source, dependent on what you found in the fields and what these women were able to bring back from the villages?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would give us only bread.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you also receive anything to -- for sleeping on, blankets, mattresses?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The women succeeded in bringing back some blankets.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there enough blankets for all 300 or so of you gathered there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How many days did these sort of conditions exist for, when you were able to do some cooking on the makeshift kitchen?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- well, the days were like eternity. We counted the nights. It must have been about a week.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during this week, did you spend every evening inside in the centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, always.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: At any stage, during those nights, were you taken to meet somebody?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would go into the big hall to meet us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said "they." Who is "they" would go into the big hall?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I did not see them, but these were uniformed persons who, at night, would enter forcibly through this door.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's the door near the number 2?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you said you didn't see this personally but what did you learn that these people came in to do?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the women who were detained in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that they would take them out as the need be.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you heard this from other detainees?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they ever give any detail as to what happened or did you just hear that women were being removed at night from that room, from that big area?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that, at night, women would be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And were you told what would happen to them after they'd been removed or people would just leave it at that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For each and every one of them was ashamed to say what.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you -- at one stage during your detention, were you taken from the place where you used to sleep at night and brought to meet some Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Roughly how many nights after the third day did this happen, if you can recall now?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was my sixth day of detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I see it's just approaching 12.30. I don't know if you want me to pause here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will take a break for 20 minutes and come back at 12.50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution can proceed. Ms. Reidy, we will have to stop the witness some 15 minutes before time. We have some issue which we must discuss in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. So that's until 1.30; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I want you now to explain to the Chamber the incident one evening where you were taken to meet some Serb soldiers. Did someone come to take you from your place where you had -- where you were sleeping?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the guards came, who took me out of the room in which I had been up to that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where did he take you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to show it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I see the map has been removed. If the witness could be shown P70.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, that night, at some point, a guard with the last name of Popovic, in full military gear, came, and there were other guards with him, even though he was the one that took me away. When he came, he told me to get up and to follow him. I asked, "Where to?" En route to where he was taking me, he said to me that he was taking me to where my role for many can be a matter of life or death. At that time, I didn't know what he meant. While he was taking me, all I could hear was prayers of women, and I will show you what direction we were heading. From the location where I lay, he took me out through this door, took me through this narrow hallway. We entered the big hall. We went downstairs. You could hear this prayer along this whole route. He took me out through this door. We went out. Nothing could be seen. You could just hear rattling of the guards' weapons, and I noticed their shadows in this area here. He took me along this route to this door here, and then he let me enter this building that is marked here with the dark shading. He took me up the stairs to a hall. From this hall, he took me to a big room for conferences or sessions. Your Honours, this was the first time in my life that I had been in these offices, and that was also the last time that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I just ask you to mark with a number 3 the entrance and place to which you were brought, where you entered and where you were taken upstairs, just so we have it permanently on the record?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. One other matter. When you said you were taken from your room, you were led through the narrow hallway and downstairs. By "downstairs," do you simply mean you came down from the podium or the steps, you didn't actually go downstairs to a basement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly right. We just went downstairs from this podium.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who was upstairs in this hallway or conference room that you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upstairs, Ranko Popovic waited for me, and another man in uniform. I know he was tall and blond but I cannot remember his name. And there, I had the opportunity to see for the first time something like that. This was the first time in my life that I saw a man wearing a fur hat who introduced himself as a Vojvoda, a duke.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This man who introduced himself as a duke, did he explain where he was from or what he was doing at the sports centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me his name was Vojvoda - that's how everybody addressed him - and that he was from Kragujevac. I noticed from his accent that he was from central Serbia. Because of the fur hat and the kokarde on the fur hat, I noticed that he was different from the other guards with whom I had the opportunity, or the misfortune, to meet up until that point. He had a huge knife, which was located by his boots, in the -- by the right arm, and his boots. He had bloodshot eyes. He was extremely tall. He said to me that his role in all of this was very important and that he had huge responsibilities and authorisation as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he ask you anything about the conditions in which you were detained or what had happened to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't ask me anything about the conditions that we were living in. He was interested in an entirely different matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What was he interested in?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was interested in the behaviour of the soldiers that, while at the time of our arrest, were taking away valuables from those that were detained.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And he questioned you about this incident, did he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His interrogation was reduced to this event. He said that his army was honourable and that he would not allow any kind of robbing in his military, and he said that his soldiers had to be punished by death if they did such a thing. It was then that I understood what Milan Popovic's words meant, and he said that the life and death of many people depended on me. Milan Popovic was the man who took me to see Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What did you tell this Vojvoda?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was extremely calm at that moment. I said that I understood that people who might have conducted themselves in such a way, and that I understood that they probably also lost somebody in this war, and I asked him to look at the situation from that perspective, that he should not punish his soldiers by death because of their temporary emotions. Your Honours, you can imagine how difficult it was for me to utter these words. I was defending somebody that I was actually -- that I should have been attacking.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you'd answered the Vojvoda in this manner, what happened next between the two of you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me, "Do you know, Jelena, that the Ustashas are slaughtering Serbian children and putting their heads into their mother's laps?" I said that I was not aware of such an act, and that I hoped that it wasn't true, but if it was, then this kind of thing should be condemned. However, that kind of action was not the fault of the soldiers and the people that were in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ask him to take any action on behalf of these sick children who were still with you at the centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our conversation was very long that night. I managed to turn a wild animal into a calm man, and I asked him politely to help the children that on that sixth day really looked terrible. I asked him if there was any possibility to bring any kind of a doctor and to administer help. He thought about it for a while and then he said that he agreed -- was agreeing to a compromise.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what compromise was that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me that he would allow the children that were the most sick to leave that area and to go to the nearest hospital, escorted by his men, under condition that my life be at any moment at their disposal. He also said to me that I would go with them but escorted by heavy guards, and in case of any kind of an incident or, God forbid, of an attack from the opposing side, I would be killed. I was happy that such a man showed some form of compassion, despite the fact that my life could have been the price.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were the children taken to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They put me in a vehicle, and the leader inside my vehicle was the police officer that followed me and took me to see Vojvoda, and I later found out that 12 children were put into the other vehicles. And we left towards the direction that at the time was unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did this happen directly after you had spoken with this Vojvoda or at a later time?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened immediately after our conversation, during the same night.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Where did the vehicles that you and the children were in eventually go to?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I talked a lot and I was very brazen, and I let it slip out that I knew which direction we were being led to because we were going fishing there very frequently. This is -- this was the road towards Pisari. We came to a private house with a huge yard, and I assume that the people that live in that house were notified by phone. After I left the car, a guard was waiting for me, and a young doctor came out who did not say his name, but he said he was from Doboj. And he said that this was a makeshift hospital for the wounded, but not a place for children. But despite that, he still admitted our children.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the children stay there or were they given some treatment and were they then returned to the sports centre in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The children were just examined at that time. They were given the most basic medical treatment, some medication. And we were all returned together to our previous residence. On the way back, I was told that the hospital had to be transferred to another location, given the fact that I had recognised where it was. So that for security purposes, they had to move it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you returned that night, did you go back to your -- the usual place where you slept?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was already dawn, and it was impossible to even think about going to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was this the only time that you had an occasion to meet this Vojvoda?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not the only occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you meet him again while you were detained in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We met again. He came to find me in the room under number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was this for another meeting or was it for some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to see whether everything was all right, and he said that I had a visitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who was that visitor?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my boyfriend, Esref Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did he allow you to meet with Esref?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He gave me 15 minutes, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: During the 15 minutes you were with Esref Kapetanovic, did he tell you whether he'd tried to make any contact with any of the defendants?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who had he tried to make contact with?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me that he went to the apartment of my neighbour, Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did he say had happened between him and Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went to ask Simo to intervene in order that I would be let free from that camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And how did Mr. Zaric respond?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he can do nothing, that it is not in his competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric knew that people were being held in Crkvina, did he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Esref bring anything to you or did you just speak with him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He brought a sleeping bag and a track suit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After this visit, approximately how many more days or nights did you spend in that centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I'm not quite sure, but I do know that I slept another -- we spent another day or two there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. After about two days, approximately, you were released from the sports centre in Crkvina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How were you told that you were being released from the sports centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been around noon on that day, I don't know exactly the day or the time, although there was some commotion and some trucks arrived, and we were told that Crkvina must be evacuated. We were told that all women residents of Samac may go home and all of those who were brought in from neighbouring villages would have to go to Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who came to tell you this information, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the head of that operation was Mr. Savo Cancar.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I just seek a clarification? Was it a Savo Cancar or a Savo Cancarevic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you're right, that his surname is Cancarevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Cancarevic from prior to your detention in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, extremely well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was he from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was not from Bosanski Samac, but he worked in the police station as a policeman, and for years we were cooperating.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in the police station of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you then put on a truck and taken back to Bosanski Samac town?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken in two rounds. I wanted to see that nobody got lost or was left behind. I ran, and when I came, the first group was already -- had already departed. When I understood that many are not being released, I asked Mr. Cancarevic, why are they being taken to Zasavica, why aren't they releasing them and letting them go home, as was our case from Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what did Mr. Cancarevic tell you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was quite clear. He took a pistol and he said, "I'm fed up with you paramilitaries." Luckily, the driver of the truck was close to him, moved his hand, and somebody who was present then helped me into the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So Mr. Cancarevic didn't offer you an explanation as to why they were being taken to Zasavica, he just expressed his anger at you by pointing his pistol at you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When this -- when the driver helped you on to the truck, did the truck then take you back to your apartment in Bosanski Samac town?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment I was put on the truck, I was given a pill to calm down, and I know that then I was got off in the street, Edvard Kardelj Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown a document? The document is document C40 from the Prosecution's exhibit list. I've distributed conies to Defence counsel and I have copies here for the Bench. I'm not leaving this topic, I just -- these are for the Bench, and if this copy which is highlighted could be shown to the witness. For the record, this document is a document dated the 15th of May, 1992. It's a document from the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac Crisis Staff, and it's a decision on the isolation of persons of Croat nationality. We've provided the Bench with both a B/C/S copy and an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps it could be marked before we discuss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is P71 ID, Your Honours, and P71 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Excuse me, could I ask the usher, perhaps the B/C/S version could be put on the ELMO? I understand that's how the defendants follow the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Although, Ms. Reidy, if the copy that's being put on the ELMO is as indistinct as the one we've been given, it's going to be very hard to read it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I appreciate that. I think the copy that has been provided is the same; everybody's in the same position. It was the quality of the copy that we were handed from -- I think, in fact, it was one of the Defence counsel who originally in 1998 handed it over to the OTP. As you can see from the translation provided, that the Translation Unit within the Tribunal were able -- have given it a full translation. And I hope that the highlighting of it makes it somewhat more clear, and I think it still may be of somewhat more use to the Defence rather than the English, if that's -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, maybe because it's difficult for you to read -- clearer for you to read from the actual document, could I just ask you to read out, as best you can, the highlighted part in the middle of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't know, it's a general objection to this. What is the relevance with this document and this witness? This is another institution, another body. I mean maybe, and probably, the Prosecution will have much more informed witnesses in this case to discuss that document. It's just a principal objection that this witness cannot give any kind of comments --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, she hasn't yet been asked about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, just in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why are you objecting?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because my learned friend, Miss Reidy, started, "Can you read the document?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why don't you let the Prosecution go ahead? Sit down, Mr. Pantelic, won't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just to prevent possible --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, Mrs. Kapetanovic, you'll see there is a section highlighted on the document, and it may be easier, more legible for you, if you can -- you can look at the document itself. Could you see if you could read that paragraph that's highlighted out slowly into the record so that we all know what the document is about?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. "Decision. With this decision, on the territory of municipality of Serbian Bosanski Samac, all members of the Croatian -- Croat people are to be isolated and distributed on the vital facilities in the town and the surroundings. The date, the 15th of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you to look at the bottom part of it? And is there any indication the source of this decision, either -- sorry. I ask you to have a look at the document and if you can tell us what the source, the people who made this decision are?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It -- what one can observe, further below, the stamp, "Bosanski Samac" and with the symbol of 4 S's, and it's clear that the source -- what the source is, it is the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I'm going to ask you to look to the top left-hand corner. I'm afraid it's not highlighted. And above the date --

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: There is the name of a body. Could you just tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac Crisis Staff. Just what I said previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, have you seen this document before arriving in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But on or around the 15th of May, you were detained from your apartment along with other persons of Croat nationality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The date is identical to that of what I have told you in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And in the time preceding the 15th of May, were you in fact isolated with other persons of Croat nationality from Bosanski Samac and from the vital facility -- and from villages around Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, to this form of question. It cannot be used the form "isolated." The other wording would be proper. It's a slightly leading question to this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a leading question, Ms. Reidy. If you can rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you, in the time period following the 15th of May, held together with other persons of Croat nationality from the territory of Bosanski Samac town and villages surrounding Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you held in a particular facility against your will?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: At any stage whilst you were there, were you able to leave the facility or return to your home?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I realise now it's half past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I can pick up on this tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness will be allowed to leave the courtroom. The evidence will be continued at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
